title: [v0.4.29] macOS: fix Darwin builds and verify build/vet
author: patplu
body:
Parent: #818 · Release context: #876 (pulled ahead of v0.4.29; target `develop`)

## Problem

`cmd/baha` does not compile for `GOOS=darwin`, so no macOS artifact can exist and every later macOS step in #822 fails at the first command. Nothing in CI detects this, so any new Linux-only line can silently re-break darwin until v0.4.29.

Evidence (current `work/v0.4.29` = `work/v0.4.25-contract-minimal-core`):

- `cmd/baha/app_backup_restore_guided.go` has no build constraint but uses Linux-only `golang.org/x/sys/unix` symbols: `unix.MemfdCreate`/`unix.MFD_CLOEXEC` (in-memory backup password file, `:572`), `unix.TCGETS`/`unix.TCSETS` termios ioctls, and passes `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` (`:591`) to the in-process password-file reader.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests on Linux only.

## Required work

1. Split the platform mechanics of `app_backup_restore_guided.go` by build constraint, keeping the guided backup/restore semantics unchanged:
   - **Linux:** existing `memfd` + `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` behavior and `TCGETS`/`TCSETS`, byte-for-byte equivalent.
   - **Darwin: Variant A — private, operation-scoped in-memory secret source (confirmed by the project owner on 2026-10-15).** The guided wrapper invokes `baseRun` in the same process; there is no backup child. Pass private secret authority directly to that operation, preserve repeated reads and existing password validation. No generated disk password file. Use platform-correct terminal control (for example `TIOCGETA`/`TIOCSETA`). Public `--password-file` remains a real owner-only regular file; do not weaken its checks to accept pipes or externally supplied handles.
   - The secret never enters logs, errors, argv or the environment on either platform.
2. Add a cheap, non-runtime CI gate to the existing `ci.yml` (no new workflow, so `scripts/ci-workflow-policy.sh` stays unchanged):
   - `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...` and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`
   - `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go vet ./...` and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./...`
3. Keep Linux unit tests and qualify the actual Darwin in-process secret handoff in the native Darwin lane (#823); cross-builds do not execute native tests. Move genuinely portable helpers such as `shellDisplayPath` into common source.

## Non-goals

- No darwin release artifact, installer or self-update change (owned by #822).
- No support-level change. Compiling on darwin does not make macOS SUPPORTED, TESTED or PORTABILITY-VERIFIED (#805/#823).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `GOOS=darwin` build and vet pass for arm64 and amd64 in `ci.yml` on every PR.
- [ ] Linux guided backup/restore behavior and tests unchanged.
- [ ] darwin password handoff writes no secret file and leaks no secret.
- [ ] Source size limits and `gofmt` pass.

## In-process secret lifetime acceptance

The earlier child-process criteria were based on an incorrect assumption and are replaced. Verified source: guided backup/restore invokes `baseRun(ctx, ...)`; `readBackupPasswordFile` uses `os.Stat`/`os.ReadFile`, requires a regular owner-only file and validates size/password. The reported native macOS descriptor measurement shares the read offset and returns empty on a second read; retain its reproduction in evidence. A pipe also fails the regular-file requirement.

- [ ] Actual guided backup/restore supports repeated authorized reads of the same validated in-memory bytes.
- [ ] No plaintext secret in argv, environment, logs, errors, machine output or generated disk password files.
- [ ] The private handle/reader is bound to the current operation, not a public token protocol or general global secret registry. Externally supplied, forged, stale, replayed or cross-operation identifiers cannot activate it.
- [ ] Public user-provided password files retain existing regular-file, permission, size and validation checks.
- [ ] Success, validation/apply failure and cancellation revoke/remove the handle and zero owned secret buffers; repeated/concurrent operations do not retain or exchange secrets.
- [ ] Terminal state is restored on completion/failure/cancellation; cleanup preserves the original error.
- [ ] Native Darwin backup/restore and race/isolation regressions qualify this adapter; encryption, consent and restore-before-mutation validation remain intact.

Variant A is approved as the implementation direction under these invariants. No generated disk-backed temporary-password fallback; explicit user-provided password files remain supported. Child-exit, broken-pipe and blocked-writer criteria do not apply to this in-process path.
